## Body

**Performance: BLOCK P197-F003** at `ef598b5437ef6a5578a2e478f358736a2e1226a4`. **P197-F001/F002 are repaired on their intended settlement paths.**

Delta from BLOCK `f105c6c`, output `ba743ff336cd9c2ca98859f97b0389170df1705b`.

**F003: tail failure precedes both settlement replay and the brake.** `notify` reads a Done/timed-out job's log at `background.rs:1429-1435` before checking the saved orphan record or classifying the owner. `read_tail` immediately propagates `File::open` failure (`:1988`); metadata/seek/read errors likewise propagate.

A Done orphan with a missing/unreadable log therefore exits before `owner_recheck_after` or `settle_braked`. No future deadline is established or renewed. Every 100 ms tick returns/decodes the job again, performs its job lookup and attempts that file open again: nominally **10 job lookups plus 10 failed opens/s**, plus shared pending selection/schema work. An already-admitted orphan record also cannot be replayed and marked notified through this early failure.

This leaves a normal filesystem-failure form of F139's forever-retry cost. The new tests use Lost jobs for the critical crash/replay cases, so they skip the tail branch. Bobcat independently reported the same source edge as correctness F004; no local/live fault injection was performed.

**Required:** allow saved settlement replay and gone-owner handling to proceed without optional completion-tail preparation blocking them; retain bounded rechecks when earlier preparation fails for a pending gone-owner job. Add a Done/timed-out, missing-log case that proves no 100 ms lookup/open storm, plus an admitted-settlement/missing-log case that completes without another notice.

**What is fixed**

- `settle_braked` renews the 60-second deadline on errors from `settle_orphan`, including failed admission/persistence/mark paths, and removes it on success. This closes the original F001 clear-before-settle error. It does not cover the earlier tail/once-guard/record-peek errors.
- The saved record is consulted before owner reclassification. An already-admitted prime leg completes from `delivery.admitted`; otherwise current prime existence/cold status is checked before a new admission, with a recorded Telegram downgrade for cold/gone. This closes F002's stale-cold replay.
- The old in-loop owner check is removed. `pending_skipping(&owner_waits(now))` is the **only selection brake**; tests exercise the query exclusion rather than hiding hydrated rows behind a second check.

**Waiting cost is reduced, not literally zero**

Between allowed looks, the SQL filter returns no waiting row, so there is no waiting-job decode, reconcile, job lookup, completion guard, owner lookup or tail attempt **when a future deadline exists**.

Each shared tick still locks/iterates the cached recheck map, clones waiting IDs, builds a dynamic `NOT IN` placeholder/SQL String and binds each ID. For W current waiters, that is O(W) list/binding work and ID bytes, plus SQLite exclusion evaluation. Pending-index entries may still be visited to reject IDs; the row-result tests are not proof of zero database page I/O. There is no list-length cap; backend bind/SQL limits and large-W cost are untested. The one live waiter is the small case.

On an allowed within-grace look with no saved settlement, the current code takes **four**, not three, logical lookup paths: job, completion once-guard, new orphan-record peek, owner. That is about **4/minute/job**, plus schema guards, history visits and any Done/timed-out tail work. Recorded replay also reads the handoff again inside `settle_orphan`. No fixed visited-row or wall-time bound is established by those method counts.

A first prime settlement may check warmth during initial route selection and again before unadmitted delivery. Replays add the admission-ledger read and only re-check current warmth when needed. These are one-time/per-allowed-attempt reads, not new per-tick owner/prime probes.

The Telegram `committed` write precedes queue enqueue, with an undo attempted on enqueue failure. This is still a non-atomic at-most-once/loss tradeoff, not proof of actual enqueue; the packet's crash-loss window and the PM/reviewer's atomic-admission concern are separate correctness matters, not cleared by this cost review.

No new executable site, timer or poll. Ordinary one-time delivery can still use existing launch adapters. Rendering changes add the existing closed/fenced helper costs, not a new schedule.
